items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: And the dean, Dean Tolles, came flying out of his office shouting

ctx.x: I think it was three hundred bucks a semester. And then you had your room and board and that depended, because it was a bad situation at Hamilton at that time. You had sixty percent of the students who were in fraternities and forty percent were not. Now if you go to a place like Harvard where they had the Persallion and the fancy clubs, only a small fracture of the student body belonged to the clubs so you could ignore them. And if you went to places where they had a universal rushing policy, where everybody had…

clear that not only was Truman likely to win but we were going to have a Democratic congress. And I don’t think it was really until six or seven in the morning that it was finally decided. And so at nine o’clock in the morning some rascal went over and rang the chapel bell, as if it had been a football victory. And the dean, Dean Tolles, came flying out of his office shouting, “God damn it, I don’t care who won the election but God damn it this is a Republican college.”
